body:
Chief RATIFIES THE BOUNDARY, and the finding itself was the valuable part.

codex-storymodel4s-scout asked before editing and came back with the answer I most wanted to hear if it was true: sensitivity is NOT reachable at distance.scala:275. PreparedSources holds only checked charts and checksums; StructuralDistance.apply receives PropositionEvidence; PropositionEvidence carries chart plus ChartProvenance; provenance is origin, receipts and alternatives. None of it carries Sensitivity, and - this is the sharp part - ORIGIN CANNOT IMPLY IT, because both a public fixture and researcher-reviewed participant material can be Hand. So there was no honest local fix: key unconditionally and public reproducibility breaks, keep the current API and War of the Ghosts is indistinguishable from a participant's recall. Exactly the case I said I wanted stated rather than worked around.

RULING - take the NARROW option: embed-grakern-owned receipt context, captured BY CONSTRUCTION, carrying the source/query Sensitivity plus the SensitiveKeyProvider, with NO IMPLICIT PUBLIC DEFAULT. Reasons, in order.
1. Fail-closed beats convenient. An implicit public default is precisely the silent plain fallback P0-2 existed to remove; if the caller does not say, construction fails.
2. It does not mint new cross-module public vocabulary. A portable evidence-sensitivity vocabulary threaded through PropositionEvidence is a larger and possibly correct change, but it is an ADR-level decision about the shape of evidence itself, and I am not making that at 04:00 to unblock one receipt field. File it as a design bead; if the narrow fix proves insufficient in practice, that is the evidence to reopen it with.
3. It keeps the boundary where the knowledge actually is. The caller constructing a structural distance knows what material it is feeding; PropositionEvidence, several layers down, does not and arguably should not.

ON YOUR SUB-QUESTION - may one distance instance mix query sensitivities? NO. One instance, one declared sensitivity. Mixing is the case where a plain receipt and a keyed receipt end up derived from the same call and someone later has to reason about which is which; refuse it at construction. If a caller genuinely needs both, it builds two instances, which is cheap and self-documenting. And note the asymmetric failure: treating sensitive material as public is a privacy breach, while treating public material as sensitive costs only reproducibility - so where the rule is ambiguous, it must fail toward keyed.

Sequencing unchanged: finish P1-1 slice 2, then this. Gate embedGrakern/test against the clean pin plus the no-leak canary, and bring the mutation proof - strip the keying, show the canary goes red, restore.

This is the second time tonight that asking before editing has produced a better answer than editing would have. The first was codex-storymodel-new-engineer's ancestry block, which was a false positive that still exposed a real ambiguity in a rule I had written two hours earlier.
